name: Index - The Swedish Contemporary Art Foundation
funding: Swedish Arts Council, City of Stockholm, Region Stockholm. Non-profit foundation returns published annually.
watch: Key Scandinavian discursive platform focusing on the role of art in society. Originating in 1974 as the underground photo magazine Bildtidningen, Index publishes critical theory, runs writing groups, and presents cutting-edge conceptual works.

name: Bergen Kunsthall
funding: Ministry of Culture, City of Bergen, Vestland county, Arts Council Norway, Fritt Ord, Sparebanken Norge, Nordic Council of Ministers, Bergesen Foundation, Westfal-Larsen fund and EGD Holding.
records_note: Its About page names 21 supporters and the 2026 board; accounts for 2023 to 2025 sit in the Norwegian register, with no annual report.

name: La Virreina Centre de la Imatge
funding: Ajuntament de Barcelona (Barcelona City Council Institute of Culture - ICUB).
watch: Public visual culture research institute housed in an 18th-century Baroque palace on La Rambla. Directed by writer and curator Valentín Roma, it champions the image as a tool of political critique and working-class emancipation.

name: Ashkal Alwan
funding: Small NGO. Major benefactors: Robert A. Matta Association, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Andy Warhol Foundation, Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Teiger Foundation; Sfeir Semler Gallery is a patron.
watch: Sharjah Art Foundation, named in the old note, is not on it.
records_note: Ashkal Alwan names four trustees and its benefactors on an undated page, but its Annual Reports section is empty and no accounts appear.

name: Printed Matter, Inc.
funding: 501(c)(3) non-profit organization funded through book distribution, NY & LA Art Book Fair fees, NYSCA, NEA, and individual donors. Board leadership is closely tied to multi-billion-dollar luxury real estate development.
watch: Longstanding Board Chair Philip Aarons is a co-founder of Millennium Partners ($4B+ luxury real estate developer) and founding chair of Friends of the High Line (the primary engine of West Chelsea/Hudson Yards hyper-gentrification and displacement). Organization has faced criticism for commercialization of the NY Art Book Fair (historic partnership with MoMA PS1), staff unionization (OPEIU Local 153) over low non-profit wages, and the co-founding legacy of Carl Andre.

name: White Columns
funding: Expenses $1.3M (FY2025). NYC DCLA and NYSCA; Warhol, Frankenthaler, Speyer, Niarchos, Luce and Blavatnik Family foundations, as listed on its 2025 support page.
watch: Blavatnik Family Foundation (Access Industries, oil origin) is contested at Tate and Oxford.
records_note: Names donors and foundations with a 2025 benefit sponsor heading and lists its board; no annual report, Form 990s for 2001 to 2025 on ProPublica.

name: Storefront for Art and Architecture
funding: 501(c)(3) non-profit organization supported by Graham Foundation, Andy Warhol Foundation, NYSCA, and individual members.

name: SOMA
funding: Civil non-profit association (Asociación Civil) funded by artist philanthropy, Fundación Jumex grants, Prince Claus Fund, and tuition-free educational patronage.
watch: Counter-institutional space founded in 2009 by a collective of artists led by Yoshua Okón.

name: Lugar a Dudas
funding: Non-profit cultural foundation supported by Prince Claus Fund, DOEN Foundation, artist philanthropy from Oscar Muñoz, and international grants.

name: Asia Art Archive (AAA)
funding: Individuals, foundations, corporate patrons, HK government agencies and an annual auction; the US arm cites NYSCA, NYC DCLA and the Ruth Foundation.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Site blocks fetches; roster still unverified.
records_note: The archive names its donors by tier and lists its board, but the site refused direct access so reports and accounts stay unchecked.

name: Raw Material Company
funding: Founded 2008 by Koyo Kouoh. Partners listed for 2024: Arts Collaboratory, OSIWA, Mellon Foundation, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Little Sun, Porticus and Sharjah Art Foundation.
watch: Operates the RAW Académie, a residency and study programme examining trans-African knowledge production and decolonial curatorial practice.
why_flagged: Founded 2008 by Koyo Kouoh. Partners listed for 2024: Arts Collaboratory, OSIWA, Mellon Foundation, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Little Sun, Porticus and Sharjah Art Foundation.
records_note: Site unreachable; its 2024 programme announcement names Arts Collaboratory, Osiwa, Mellon, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Little Sun, Porticus and Sharjah Art Foundation.

name: CCA Lagos (Centre for Contemporary Art)
funding: Founded 2007 by Bisi Silva with her own money. A March 2022 Sotheby's benefit auction raised US$1M toward a permanent home in Yaba. It publishes no funder list.
watch: Founded in 2007 by the visionary curator Bisi Silva to prioritize visual art research, experimental installation, and photography in Nigeria. Operates the Asiko International Art School and one of West Africa's largest visual art libraries.
records_note: Its site names its trustees and staff, but posts no annual report, accounts or funder list.
